close_reason:
Wontfix.

The bead is correctly self-labeled 'opinion' and concludes 'P2 because all current targets are 64-bit and the cast is correct today.' That's the workspace's bikeshedding signal: a finding that has engineering basis in principle but no measurable defect on any platform that exists.

Two paths the bead suggests both have problems:

1. 'u64::try_from(x.len()).expect("usize fits in u64 on supported targets")' — workspace AGENTS.md explicitly forbids .expect() in library code ('No .unwrap() or .expect() in library code — propagate errors with ?'). Adopting this pattern would replace a silent-correctness-on-all-current-targets cast with an explicit panic-on-impossible-target. The panic IS the silent truncation made loud, but it adds ceremony for no measurable benefit when no supported target can trigger it.

2. Helper fn usize_to_u64 — centralizes but does not change the panic semantic. Still violates the no-expect rule.

Path 3 (not in the bead): switch every cap field from u64 to usize. That works structurally — the field declarations and the comparison happen in the same type — but flips the ClientError::ResponseTooLarge variant payload to usize, which IS a public-API breaking change and we have specifically deferred those (see JMAP-6r7c.50 / .48 / .20 escalation comments). Disproportionate for an opinion-labeled finding.

If a supported target ever changes to >64-bit usize, the cast will need a fix bead at that time AND the broader workspace will likely require similar fixes everywhere u64 caps interact with byte-vector lengths (jmap-server, jmap-mime, mime-tree, several extension servers). A workspace-wide sweep at that point is more coherent than a per-crate change today.

description: crate-jmap-base-client/src/{client.rs:280,282,334,336},{blob.rs:237,263,265,376} all do 'bytes.len() as u64' or 'data.len() as u64' as part of the size-cap-check pattern. On every 64-bit platform usize is u64, so the 'as u64' is a lossless reinterpret. On any future platform where usize > 64 bits (real for some 128-bit address-space targets reqwest may eventually be built on), 'as u64' silently truncates and the size-cap check would let an oversized response pass. The idiomatic shape is u64::try_from(bytes.len()).unwrap_or(u64::MAX) for the comparison (or saturate-on-overflow), or — since the value flows directly into ClientError::ResponseTooLarge { actual: u64, limit: u64 } — using usize-typed limits everywhere and casting at the API boundary only once. The 'as u64' cast in transport-size-check code is exactly the pattern that bites years later when someone reads the limit definition (u64) and the body buffer (Vec<u8>::len() -> usize) and assumes the cast is documented somewhere. clippy::cast_possible_truncation flags this lint at the pedantic level. Recommendation: replace each 'x.len() as u64' with 'u64::try_from(x.len()).expect("usize fits in u64 on supported targets")' or pull a tiny helper fn usize_to_u64(n: usize) -> u64 { n.try_into().expect(...) } and document the supported-target invariant in one place. P2 because all current targets are 64-bit and the cast is correct today.
title: bytes.len() as u64 cast appears 5 times in transport size-cap checks — fragile + lossy on 128-bit hosts
